task: Draft a five-question FAQ section for a fictional clinic's patient portal covering a routine blood panel. Answer each question in one to three sentences. Questions: (1) What does the panel measure? (2) How do I read my result report? (3) When will my results be available? (4) Who will explain my results? (5) What should I do if I am worried about a result? No diagnosis, no specific marker values, no treatment recommendations. Use plain language suitable for a general adult reader.

facts.text: The FAQ covers a fictional routine blood panel offered at Lakeview Clinic.
The panel measures markers across several categories as listed in the clinic's order form; the specific markers are not reproduced in the FAQ.
Individual normal ranges vary by laboratory; the ranges that apply to each patient are printed on the patient's own result report, not in the FAQ.
A clinician reviews the result before it is shared with the patient.
Results are available through the patient's online portal within two to three business days of the sample being received at the laboratory.
Result reports include flags (H for above range, L for below range) beside each value; these flags reflect the laboratory's reference ranges and are not a clinical interpretation.
Patients with concerns about a result should contact the clinic by phone; they should not attend an emergency department for routine blood panel queries.
The FAQ entry is not a diagnostic tool and does not replace a clinical consultation.

forbidden_additions: A diagnosis or clinical interpretation of any specific marker value.
A stated normal range beyond the note that ranges are printed on the result report.
A treatment recommendation, referral instruction, or emergency guidance beyond the supplied contact-clinic direction.
preserve: The attribution of normal ranges to the patient's own result report, not the FAQ.
The two-to-three business-day result availability period.
The H/L flag explanation as a laboratory reference indicator, not a clinical verdict.
The instruction to contact the clinic by phone for concerns, not an emergency department.
